title: atago project manifest
description: Directory-level configuration for a tree of atago specs (#392). Named atago.project.yaml and discovered from a spec's own location by walking up to the nearest one, so `atago run ./e2e` and `atago run ./e2e/one.atago.yaml` resolve the same configuration. It carries what belongs to a DIRECTORY rather than to a file — shared defaults, shared environment, and the committed fixture tree — and never scenario definitions: it is configuration, not composition.

env.description: Environment variables for every spec under this directory. The weakest layer: host < project < suite < scenario < step, so any level below may override a key.

defaults.description: Default fragments merged beneath every matching element of every spec under this directory, with the same rules a spec file's own `defaults:` uses (#39): an explicit value always wins, maps shallow-merge, and a spec file's own defaults: beat these.

fixtures_dir.description: A committed fixture tree, resolved relative to this manifest's directory (absolute paths allowed) and exposed to every spec under it as ${fixtures} (#394). It is checked to exist at load time, so a typo is one message about the manifest rather than N per-scenario failures about a missing file. Treat it as read-only input: steps write into ${workdir}.

subject.description: The binary under test (#393): how to build it, and what specs call it. The build runs ONCE per `atago run` invocation, before any scenario, and the artifact's directory is prepended to PATH so a bare name in a spec resolves to the freshly built binary. Deliberately language-neutral — a build is just a command.

name.description: What specs call the binary. On Windows the artifact resolves with a .exe suffix automatically.

artifact.description: Where the build writes, relative to a run-scoped scratch directory (never into the repository). ${artifact} in the build command expands to its absolute path.

build.description: The command that produces the artifact.

additionalProperties.description: A named build variation selected with `atago run --profile NAME`. It must set build, env, or both.

build.description: Replaces the subject's build command wholly while this profile is active. Whole-command replacement rather than a merge: a half-merged build command is unpredictable.

env.description: Environment layered into the build and into every spec under the manifest while this profile is active. This is where a coverage run passes GOCOVERDIR or LLVM_PROFILE_FILE — atago knows nothing about either; merging the raw profiles afterwards stays a toolchain job.

profiles.description: Named build variations (#393), e.g. a coverage-instrumented build. Without --profile the plain subject.build runs, so the default path is unchanged.

command.description: The build command. ${artifact} expands to the absolute output path. Parsed as argv unless shell is set.

shell.description: Run the command through a shell, for a build that needs shell syntax.

cwd.description: Where the build runs, relative to the manifest's directory. A manifest under e2e/ usually builds from the module root above it.

timeout.description: Go duration bounding the build (default 10m). A hung build must fail the run rather than the CI job's wall clock.
